summary: Rob Nairn (1939–2023) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Zimbabwe, King's College London, the University of London, and the University of Edinburgh. He served as senior lecturer at Zimbabwe and professor at Cape Town (~1977–1981).

Robert A. F. Thurman (1941–2026) specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Harvard, under Ngawang Wangyal, and under Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale. He was president of the American Institute of Buddhist Studies and Tibet House US, and taught at Amherst and Columbia.
Robert Alan Goodding is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Texas at Austin in 2002, where he studied under Patrick Olivelle.

Robert Alexander Neil (1852–1901) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Aberdeen under William Duguid Geddes and at Peterhouse under several scholars, including E. B. Cowell. Neil lectured in Sanskrit at Cambridge and was a Fellow and Senior Tutor at Pembroke College.

Robert Anthony Orsi (born 1953) works in religious studies and history. After studying at Trinity College and Yale, he held posts at Fordham, Indiana University, Harvard, Northwestern University (from ~2007), and the University of Notre Dame (2020–2021).

Robert B. Ekvall (1898–1983) was a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He held research appointments at the University of Chicago (~1953–1958) and the University of Washington (1958), and was an honorary curator at the Burke Museum (~1958–1983).

Robert Baker Aitken (1917–2010) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi, UC Berkeley, Ryutaku-ji, and under teachers including D. T. Suzuki and Soen Nakagawa. He held posts at Hawaiʻi and the East-West Center.

Robert Barnett (born 1953) is a Tibetologist who studied at Cambridge. He directed the Tibet University summer program (2000–2006) and held posts at Columbia University (~1999–2018), SOAS (~2018), and King's College London.

Robert Caesar Childers (1838–1876) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Oxford, Wadham College, and under Yātrāmullē Dhammārāma. He was a sub-librarian at the India Office (1872) and a professor of Pâli at University College London (~1872–1876).

Robert Chalmers (1858–1938) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Oriel College, Oxford, and under T. W. Rhys Davids, he later served as president of the Royal Asiatic Society (1922–1925) and Master of Peterhouse (1924–1931).

Robert Chambers (1737–1803) was an Oxford-educated legal scholar and Indologist. He served as Vinerian Professor of English Law at Oxford and Principal of New Inn Hall (1766), Chief Justice at Fort William (~1791–1798), and president of The Asiatic Society (~1797–1798).

Robert Charles Zaehner (1913–1974) was a religious studies, Iranian, and Indology scholar. He studied at Christ Church and Cambridge under Harold Walter Bailey. He held posts in the Secret Intelligence Service and served as Spalding Professor at Oxford from 1952.

Robert DeCaroli (born 1970) specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and art history. He earned his MA and PhD at UCLA, studying under Robert L. Brown. After lecturing at UCLA and Loyola Marymount, he joined the George Mason University faculty in ~1999.

Robert Deliège (born 1953) is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Oxford (~1978–1984) and has held academic posts at the University of Kerala and UCLouvain (since ~1989).

Robert Duquenne is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a specialist in Tantric Buddhism for Hōbōgirin (attested 1891) and was affiliated with the École Française d'Extrême-Orient (attested 2009).

Robert E. Buswell Jr. (born 1953) is a Buddhist studies scholar. He trained under Kusan Sunim and completed his AB, MA, and PhD at UC Berkeley under Lewis Lancaster and others, later serving as professor at UCLA (~1986–2022).

Robert E. Morrell is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Robert H. Brower and William H. McCullough and held a post at Washington University in St. Louis (attested 1985 and 2006).

Robert E. Svoboda (born 1953) is an Indologist who studied at the University of Oklahoma and mentored under Vimalananda (~1975–1983). He has been an adjunct member at The Ayurvedic Institute, Bastyr University, and the Institute for Religion and Health.

Robert F. Rhodes works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. A doctoral candidate at Harvard University, he has served as a professor at Otani University (attested 1993–1997, 2012–2014) and was a committee member for the Otani Academic Society.

Robert Florida is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He served as Dean of Arts and Professor of Religion at Brandon University and later as an Emeritus Fellow at the University of Victoria (attested 2000–2005).
